mainEntity.name: How much does a Nissan Juke 1.6 DIG-T Nismo engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A reconditioned Nissan Juke 1.6 DIG-T Nismo (MR16DDT) engine typically costs between £1,800 and £3,000 for the unit alone, while a fully rebuilt unit ranges from £2,500 to £3,500.

mainEntity.name: What are the common problems with the Nissan Juke MR16DDT engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The MR16DDT in the Nissan Juke 1.6 DIG-T Nismo is prone to timing chain stretch and tensioner failure, which can lead to rod bearing wear. Blocked turbo oil feed lines are also a known issue, causing oil starvation.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Nissan Juke 1.6 DIG-T Nismo?

acceptedAnswer.text: With current market values for the F15 Juke Nismo ranging from £6,000 to £14,000, the decision depends on the vehicle's overall condition. If the car is worth under £5,000, a used engine or targeted repair is often more financially sensible.

mainEntity.name: Will a standard Nissan Juke 1.6 DIG-T engine fit my Nismo?

acceptedAnswer.text: While the standard MR16DDT block shares physical dimensions with the Nismo variant, a direct swap is not plug-and-play. The Nismo uses specific ECU mapping, a larger turbocharger, and different exhaust manifolds.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Nissan Juke 1.6 DIG-T Nismo engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional supply and fit service for the MR16DDT engine typically takes 1 to 2 days. The R&R (remove and replace) labour time is estimated at 8 to 11 hours by UK specialists.

mainEntity.name: What warranty is included with a rebuilt Nissan Juke Nismo engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every rebuilt or reconditioned Nissan Juke 1.6 DIG-T Nismo engine supplied through EnginesMarket carries a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

historyTimeline.intro: When the 1.6 DIG-T Nismo variant launched, it brought rally-inspired performance to the Juke range, utilising a heavily modified version of the MR16DDT engine block. Over its production run, this variant saw a power increase with the limited-run Nismo RS, but retained the same core 1.6-litre turbocharged architecture.

problems.rootCause: Timing chain tensioner wear and blocked turbo oil feed lines can lead to oil starvation, causing premature rod bearing wear and eventual catastrophic bottom-end failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Timing chain kit and oil pump replacement.
repairOptions.longevity: Viable only if caught early with no bottom-end damage.
